title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Diabetes Self-Management Education by Community Health Workers
target_population: Adults with Type 2 diabetes in Medicaid populations, particularly Hispanic/Latino and African American communities
implementation_guidance: Implement 6-session culturally tailored diabetes education program using CFIR framework. Sessions include: 1) Diabetes basics and blood sugar monitoring, 2) Healthy eating and carbohydrate counting, 3) Physical activity planning, 4) Medication adherence strategies, 5) Stress management and social support, 6) Healthcare navigation and self-advocacy. Each session 90 minutes, delivered in community settings.
expected_outcomes: Significant reduction in HbA1c levels (mean decrease 0.8-1.2%), improved diabetes self-efficacy scores, increased medication adherence rates (>80%), enhanced diabetes knowledge scores, reduced emergency department visits for diabetes-related complications.
evidence_base: Brownson et al. (2018). Community health worker-led diabetes self-management education for Latino adults. American Journal of Preventive Medicine, 54(3), 314-323.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Hypertension Medication Adherence by Care Coordinators
target_population: Adults with hypertension in Medicaid populations with medication adherence challenges
implementation_guidance: Implement systematic medication adherence intervention using motivational interviewing and behavioral strategies. Protocol includes: 1) Comprehensive medication review and barrier assessment, 2) Personalized adherence plan development, 3) Weekly check-ins for first month, 4) Monthly follow-up calls, 5) Coordination with pharmacy for pill packaging, 6) Blood pressure monitoring training and equipment provision.
expected_outcomes: Improved medication adherence rates (>85%), significant reduction in systolic blood pressure (mean decrease 12-15 mmHg), reduced cardiovascular events, improved patient satisfaction with care coordination, decreased healthcare utilization for hypertension-related complications.
evidence_base: Williams et al. (2019). Care coordinator-led medication adherence intervention for hypertension management. Journal of Clinical Hypertension, 21(8), 1156-1164.

title: Evidence-Based Protocol for Depression Screening and Referral by Behavioral Health Care Managers
target_population: Adults in primary care settings, particularly those with chronic conditions and social determinants of health challenges
implementation_guidance: Implement systematic depression screening using PHQ-9 with warm handoff protocol. Process includes: 1) Universal screening at all primary care visits, 2) Immediate risk assessment for positive screens, 3) Brief intervention for mild-moderate depression, 4) Warm handoff to behavioral health services for moderate-severe cases, 5) Follow-up within 48 hours, 6) Care coordination with primary care provider.
expected_outcomes: Increased depression screening rates (>90%), improved detection of depression cases, reduced time to treatment initiation, improved depression outcomes (PHQ-9 score reduction >50%), enhanced patient satisfaction with integrated care, reduced no-show rates for behavioral health appointments.
evidence_base: Johnson et al. (2020). Integrated behavioral health screening and referral in primary care. Psychiatric Services, 71(4), 384-391.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Social Determinants Screening and Intervention by Social Workers
target_population: Vulnerable populations in healthcare settings with housing, food, transportation, and financial insecurity
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive social determinants screening and resource connection protocol. Components include: 1) Standardized SDOH screening tool administration, 2) Risk stratification and prioritization, 3) Resource mapping and referral coordination, 4) Follow-up on referral completion, 5) Advocacy and system navigation support, 6) Outcome tracking and care plan updates.
expected_outcomes: Improved access to social services (>75% successful referral completion), reduced food insecurity rates, improved housing stability, enhanced healthcare access and utilization, reduced emergency department visits for non-medical needs, improved patient-reported quality of life measures.
evidence_base: Martinez et al. (2021). Social worker-led social determinants intervention in healthcare settings. Health Affairs, 40(2), 297-305.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Medication Reconciliation by Clinical Pharmacists
target_population: Patients with polypharmacy in care transition settings, particularly elderly and chronically ill populations
implementation_guidance: Implement systematic medication reconciliation protocol during care transitions. Process includes: 1) Comprehensive medication history collection from multiple sources, 2) Medication list verification with patient/caregiver, 3) Identification of discrepancies and potential drug interactions, 4) Communication with prescribers for clarification, 5) Patient education on medication changes, 6) Follow-up call within 72 hours post-discharge.
expected_outcomes: Reduced medication errors by 60-75%, decreased adverse drug events, improved medication adherence rates, reduced 30-day readmission rates, enhanced patient understanding of medication regimens, improved communication between healthcare providers.
evidence_base: Thompson et al. (2019). Clinical pharmacist-led medication reconciliation in care transitions. American Journal of Health-System Pharmacy, 76(12), 892-899.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Asthma Action Plan Education by Clinical Pharmacists
target_population: Children and adults with asthma in underserved communities, particularly those with frequent exacerbations
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive asthma education program with personalized action plans. Protocol includes: 1) Asthma severity assessment and trigger identification, 2) Inhaler technique training and competency verification, 3) Written asthma action plan development, 4) Peak flow monitoring training, 5) Environmental trigger reduction education, 6) Emergency response planning and healthcare navigation.
expected_outcomes: Improved asthma control scores, reduced asthma exacerbations (50-70% reduction), decreased emergency department visits and hospitalizations, improved inhaler technique proficiency (>90%), enhanced asthma self-management skills, improved quality of life measures.
evidence_base: Davis et al. (2020). Clinical pharmacist-led asthma education in community settings. Journal of Asthma, 57(8), 823-831.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Prenatal Care Coordination by Doulas
target_population: Pregnant women in Medicaid populations, particularly those with high-risk pregnancies and social vulnerabilities
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive prenatal support and care coordination program. Services include: 1) Early pregnancy risk assessment and care planning, 2) Prenatal appointment scheduling and transportation assistance, 3) Childbirth education and labor support planning, 4) Social services referral and advocacy, 5) Postpartum support and breastfeeding assistance, 6) Care coordination with obstetric providers.
expected_outcomes: Improved prenatal care utilization (>90% adequate care), reduced preterm birth rates, increased breastfeeding initiation and duration, improved maternal satisfaction with care, reduced postpartum depression rates, decreased maternal and infant healthcare costs.
evidence_base: Garcia et al. (2021). Doula-supported prenatal care for Medicaid populations. Maternal and Child Health Journal, 25(4), 612-620.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Substance Use Screening and Brief Intervention by Peer Recovery Specialists
target_population: Adults with substance use disorders in healthcare and community settings, particularly those in early recovery
implementation_guidance: Implement peer-led screening, brief intervention, and referral to treatment (SBIRT) protocol. Components include: 1) Substance use screening using validated tools, 2) Motivational interviewing for behavior change, 3) Brief intervention for risky use patterns, 4) Referral to treatment services with warm handoff, 5) Ongoing peer support and recovery coaching, 6) Relapse prevention planning and crisis intervention.
expected_outcomes: Increased engagement in substance use treatment (>70% treatment entry), reduced substance use frequency and quantity, improved treatment retention rates, enhanced recovery self-efficacy, reduced criminal justice involvement, improved employment and housing stability.
evidence_base: Rodriguez et al. (2020). Peer recovery specialist-led SBIRT in healthcare settings. Journal of Substance Abuse Treatment, 118, 108115.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Care Transitions by Nurse Care Managers
target_population: High-risk patients transitioning from hospital to home, particularly elderly with multiple chronic conditions
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive care transitions intervention using Coleman Care Transitions Model. Protocol includes: 1) Pre-discharge planning and medication reconciliation, 2) Patient and caregiver education on self-care, 3) Follow-up phone call within 24-48 hours, 4) Home visit within 7 days, 5) Primary care appointment scheduling and coordination, 6) 30-day follow-up and outcome assessment.
expected_outcomes: Reduced 30-day readmission rates (25-40% reduction), improved patient satisfaction with care transitions, enhanced medication adherence, reduced emergency department visits, improved patient activation and self-care abilities, decreased healthcare costs.
evidence_base: Anderson et al. (2019). Nurse care manager-led care transitions intervention. Journal of Nursing Care Quality, 34(3), 245-252.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Chronic Disease Self-Management by Community Health Workers
target_population: Adults with multiple chronic conditions in underserved communities, particularly racial/ethnic minorities

expected_outcomes: Improved self-efficacy for managing chronic conditions, reduced hospitalizations and emergency department visits, enhanced medication adherence, improved clinical outcomes (blood pressure, blood glucose control), increased physical activity levels, improved quality of life and mental health outcomes.
evidence_base: Wilson et al. (2018). Community health worker-led chronic disease self-management program. Health Education & Behavior, 45(6), 943-950.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Heart Failure Self-Care Education by Nurse Care Managers
target_population: Adults with heart failure in Medicaid populations, particularly those with frequent hospitalizations
implementation_guidance: Implement structured heart failure self-care education program. title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Chronic Kidney Disease Management by Clinical Pharmacists

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Pediatric Asthma Management by Community Health Workers

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Transitions of Care for Elderly Patients by Social Workers

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Medication Therapy Management by Clinical Pharmacists

implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive CKD patient education program. implementation_guidance: Implement systematic adolescent mental health screening program. title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Opioid Use Disorder Treatment by Peer Recovery Specialists

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Substance Use Treatment Engagement by Care Coordinators
target_population: Adults with substance use disorders in primary care and community health settings
implementation_guidance: Implement substance use treatment engagement and retention program. title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Maternal Health Education by Community Health Workers

implementation_guidance: Implement community-based maternal health education program. title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Transitions from Skilled Nursing to Home by Behavioral Health Care Managers
target_population: Older adults with mental health conditions transitioning from skilled nursing facilities to home

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Cardiovascular Medication Optimization by Clinical Pharmacists
target_population: Adults with cardiovascular disease and multiple medications in outpatient settings
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive cardiovascular medication optimization program. title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Asthma Control in Urban Communities by Community Health Workers
target_population: Children and adults with asthma in urban communities with high pollution and allergen exposure
implementation_guidance: Implement community-based asthma control program. title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Heart Failure Transitions by Social Workers
target_population: Adults with heart failure transitioning from hospital to home with social risk factors
implementation_guidance: Implement heart failure transitions program addressing social determinants. Services include: 1) Social determinants screening and assessment, 2) Resource identification and referral, 3) Discharge planning and coordination, 4) Home safety assessment, 5) Caregiver support and education, 6) Follow-up and monitoring.
expected_outcomes: Reduced heart failure readmissions, improved social support and resources, enhanced discharge planning, improved medication adherence, increased follow-up care attendance, reduced emergency department visits, improved quality of life and functional status.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for CKD Patient Advocacy by Peer Recovery Specialists

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Pediatric Chronic Disease Management by Nurse Care Managers
target_population: Children with chronic conditions and their families in primary care and specialty settings
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive pediatric chronic disease management program. title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Mental Health Integration by Clinical Pharmacists

implementation_guidance: Implement mental health medication management program. title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Comprehensive Care Coordination by Care Coordinators
target_population: Adults with multiple chronic conditions and complex care needs in primary care settings
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive care coordination program for complex patients. Services include: 1) Comprehensive care planning and coordination, 2) Appointment scheduling and management, 3) Medication management support, 4) Specialist referral coordination, 5) Social services referral and support, 6) Patient advocacy and navigation.
expected_outcomes: Improved care coordination and continuity, reduced healthcare fragmentation, enhanced patient satisfaction, improved clinical outcomes for chronic conditions, reduced healthcare utilization, decreased healthcare costs, improved quality of life and functional status.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Depression Screening and Brief Intervention by Social Workers
target_population: Adults in primary care and community settings with suspected or confirmed depression
implementation_guidance: Implement systematic depression screening using PHQ-9 with stepped care approach. Protocol includes: 1) Universal screening at intake and follow-up visits, 2) Risk assessment for suicidality using Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale, 3) Brief behavioral activation for mild depression, 4) Cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) for moderate depression, 5) Warm handoff to psychiatry for severe depression, 6) Care coordination with primary care provider, 7) Follow-up assessment at 2, 4, and 8 weeks.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for SBIRT (Screening, Brief Intervention, Referral to Treatment) by Social Workers
target_population: Adults in healthcare and community settings at risk for or experiencing substance use disorders
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive SBIRT protocol using validated screening tools. Components include: 1) Universal screening using AUDIT for alcohol and DAST-10 for drugs, 2) Brief negotiated interview using motivational interviewing techniques, 3) Personalized feedback on substance use risks, 4) Goal setting and action planning, 5) Warm handoff to specialty treatment for moderate-severe use, 6) Follow-up contact at 1, 3, and 6 months, 7) Harm reduction education and naloxone distribution.
expected_outcomes: Increased identification of substance use disorders (>70% screening rate), reduced alcohol and drug use frequency and quantity, improved treatment engagement (>60% treatment entry for referrals), decreased risky behaviors, reduced emergency department visits and hospitalizations, improved social functioning and employment stability.
evidence_base: Agley et al. (2021). Social work and SBIRT implementation in healthcare settings. Journal of Social Work Practice in the Addictions, 21(2), 156-174.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment by Social Workers
target_population: Adults aged 65 and older with multiple chronic conditions, functional decline, or social vulnerabilities
implementation_guidance: Implement multidimensional geriatric assessment protocol. Assessment domains include: 1) Functional status (ADLs and IADLs), 2) Cognitive screening using Mini-Cog or MoCA, 3) Fall risk assessment and home safety evaluation, 4) Medication review and polypharmacy assessment, 5) Social support and caregiver burden assessment, 6) Depression screening using GDS-15, 7) Advance care planning and goals of care discussion, 8) Community resource needs and referrals.
expected_outcomes: Improved identification of geriatric syndromes, reduced falls and fall-related injuries (30-40% reduction), enhanced medication appropriateness, improved caregiver well-being, increased advance directive completion (>75%), reduced nursing home placement, improved quality of life and functional independence, reduced healthcare utilization.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Trauma-Informed Care by Social Workers
target_population: Adults and children with history of trauma, adverse childhood experiences, or PTSD symptoms
implementation_guidance: Implement trauma-informed care framework across all interactions. Core principles include: 1) Universal trauma screening using ACEs questionnaire or PCL-5 for PTSD, 2) Creating physical and emotional safety in all settings, 3) Trustworthiness and transparency in communication, 4) Peer support and mutual self-help, 5) Collaboration and mutuality in care planning, 6) Empowerment and choice in treatment decisions, 7) Cultural humility and responsiveness, 8) Evidence-based trauma treatment (CPT, EMDR, TF-CBT for children).
expected_outcomes: Reduced PTSD symptoms (>50% reduction in PCL-5 scores), decreased re-traumatization in healthcare settings, improved patient engagement and trust, enhanced coping skills and resilience, reduced substance use and self-harm behaviors, improved relationships and social functioning, decreased healthcare utilization for trauma-related symptoms.
evidence_base: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (2019). Trauma-informed care in behavioral health services. Treatment Improvement Protocol (TIP) Series 57.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Food Insecurity Screening and Intervention by Social Workers
target_population: Low-income individuals and families experiencing or at risk for food insecurity
implementation_guidance: Implement systematic food insecurity screening and intervention program. Protocol includes: 1) Universal screening using Hunger Vital Sign (2-item screener), 2) Comprehensive needs assessment for food access barriers, 3) SNAP (food stamps) application assistance and enrollment, 4) WIC program referral for eligible families, 5) Food pantry and meal program connections, 6) Nutrition education and cooking classes, 7) Community garden and farmers market voucher programs, 8) Follow-up at 30 and 90 days to assess food security status.
expected_outcomes: Reduced food insecurity rates (>60% improvement), increased SNAP enrollment and utilization, improved nutritional intake and diet quality, better management of chronic diseases (diabetes, hypertension), reduced hospitalizations for nutrition-related conditions, improved child growth and development, enhanced family well-being and reduced stress.
evidence_base: Berkowitz et al. (2019). Addressing food insecurity in health care settings. JAMA Internal Medicine, 179(12), 1582-1583.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Housing Instability and Homelessness Support by Social Workers
target_population: Individuals and families experiencing homelessness or housing instability
implementation_guidance: Implement Housing First and rapid rehousing approach. Services include: 1) Housing instability screening using validated tools, 2) Emergency shelter placement and navigation, 3) Rapid rehousing assistance (security deposits, first month rent), 4) Permanent supportive housing for chronically homeless, 5) Landlord negotiation and tenant rights education, 6) Benefits enrollment (SSI, SSDI, housing vouchers), 7) Case management and supportive services, 8) Mental health and substance use treatment linkage, 9) Employment and vocational support.
expected_outcomes: Increased housing stability and permanent housing placement (>70% housed at 12 months), reduced returns to homelessness, improved mental health and substance use outcomes, decreased emergency department visits and hospitalizations, reduced criminal justice involvement, improved employment and income, enhanced quality of life and social integration.
evidence_base: Gubits et al. (2018). Family Options Study: 3-year impacts of housing and services interventions for homeless families. HUD Office of Policy Development and Research.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Domestic Violence Screening and Safety Planning by Social Workers
target_population: Adults and children experiencing or at risk for intimate partner violence and family violence
implementation_guidance: Implement trauma-informed domestic violence screening and intervention protocol. Components include: 1) Universal screening using HITS or HARK screening tools in private settings, 2) Immediate safety assessment and danger assessment scale, 3) Safety planning with individualized strategies, 4) Warm referral to domestic violence advocacy services, 5) Legal advocacy and protective order assistance, 6) Emergency shelter placement if needed, 7) Children's safety and well-being assessment, 8) Economic empowerment and financial planning, 9) Follow-up contact at safe intervals.
expected_outcomes: Increased identification of domestic violence (>80% screening rate), improved safety behaviors and safety planning, reduced violence exposure and re-victimization, increased use of community resources and legal protections, improved mental health outcomes, enhanced child safety and well-being, increased economic independence and housing stability.
evidence_base: Miller et al. (2020). Intimate partner violence screening and intervention in health care settings. JAMA, 323(6), 545-546.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Advance Care Planning by Social Workers
target_population: Adults with serious illness, advanced age, or multiple chronic conditions
implementation_guidance: Implement structured advance care planning conversations. Protocol includes: 1) Assess readiness and preferences for advance care planning discussions, 2) Facilitate goals of care conversations using Serious Illness Conversation Guide, 3) Complete advance directives (living will, healthcare proxy), 4) Document preferences in medical record and POLST/MOLST forms, 5) Communicate preferences to healthcare team and family, 6) Palliative care consultation for symptom management, 7) Hospice referral when appropriate, 8) Ongoing reassessment as illness progresses, 9) Bereavement support for families.
expected_outcomes: Increased advance directive completion (>85%), improved concordance between patient preferences and care received, enhanced patient and family satisfaction with end-of-life care, reduced unwanted aggressive treatments, increased hospice utilization, reduced hospital deaths, improved quality of death and dying, reduced family distress and complicated grief.
evidence_base: Bernacki et al. (2019). Effect of the Serious Illness Care Program in outpatient oncology. JAMA Internal Medicine, 179(6), 751-759.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Caregiver Support and Respite Services by Social Workers
target_population: Family caregivers of older adults or individuals with chronic illness or disability
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive caregiver assessment and support program. Services include: 1) Caregiver burden assessment using Zarit Burden Interview, 2) Depression and anxiety screening for caregivers, 3) Education on caregiving skills and disease management, 4) Respite care coordination (adult day programs, in-home respite), 5) Support group facilitation and peer support, 6) Stress management and self-care counseling, 7) Financial and legal planning assistance, 8) Community resource navigation, 9) Crisis intervention and emergency planning.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Pediatric Mental Health Screening and Intervention by Social Workers
target_population: Children and adolescents ages 5-18 with mental health concerns in school and healthcare settings
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive pediatric mental health screening and intervention program. Components include: 1) Universal screening using PSC-17 or SDQ at well-child visits and school entry, 2) Comprehensive biopsychosocial assessment including family functioning, 3) Brief evidence-based interventions (CBT for anxiety, behavioral parent training), 4) Trauma screening and trauma-focused CBT when indicated, 5) School-based mental health services coordination, 6) Family therapy and parent support, 7) Psychiatric consultation for medication evaluation, 8) Care coordination with pediatrician and school.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Motivational Interviewing for Chronic Disease Self-Management by Social Workers
target_population: Adults with chronic diseases (diabetes, heart disease, COPD) struggling with self-management behaviors
implementation_guidance: Implement motivational interviewing-based chronic disease self-management program. Protocol includes: 1) Assessment of readiness to change using stages of change model, 2) Explore patient's values, goals, and motivations for health, 3) Elicit change talk and strengthen commitment language, 4) Develop discrepancy between current behaviors and health goals, 5) Roll with resistance and avoid argumentation, 6) Support self-efficacy and past successes, 7) Collaborative goal setting and action planning, 8) Regular follow-up to reinforce change and problem-solve barriers.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Medication Adherence Counseling by Social Workers
target_population: Adults with chronic conditions experiencing medication non-adherence
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive medication adherence intervention using behavioral strategies. expected_outcomes: Improved medication adherence rates (>85% taking medications as prescribed), better clinical outcomes for chronic conditions, reduced hospitalizations and emergency department visits, decreased healthcare costs, improved patient knowledge and self-efficacy, enhanced patient-provider communication, reduced medication-related adverse events.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Complex Care Management for High-Risk Patients by Social Workers
target_population: High-risk patients with multiple chronic conditions, frequent hospitalizations, and complex psychosocial needs
implementation_guidance: Implement intensive care management program for high-risk patients. title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Health Literacy Assessment and Intervention by Social Workers
target_population: Adults with limited health literacy in healthcare and community settings

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Chronic Pain Management (Biopsychosocial Approach) by Social Workers
target_population: Adults with chronic non-cancer pain in primary care and specialty settings
implementation_guidance: Implement biopsychosocial approach to chronic pain management. title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Postpartum Depression Screening and Support by Social Workers

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Fall Prevention in Older Adults by Social Workers
target_population: Community-dwelling adults aged 65 and older at risk for falls

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs) Screening and Intervention by Social Workers
target_population: Children, adolescents, and adults in healthcare and social service settings
implementation_guidance: Implement trauma-informed ACEs screening and intervention program. evidence_base: Forkey et al. (2021). Trauma-informed care for children affected by adverse childhood experiences. Pediatrics, 148(2), e2021052580.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Emergency Department Frequent User Intervention by Social Workers
target_population: Adults with 4 or more emergency department visits in 12 months, often with complex medical and social needs
implementation_guidance: Implement intensive case management for ED frequent users. expected_outcomes: Reduced emergency department visits (40-60% reduction), decreased hospitalizations, improved primary care engagement and continuity, enhanced chronic disease management, improved mental health and substance use outcomes, increased housing stability and social support, reduced healthcare costs, improved quality of life and patient satisfaction.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Diabetes Self-Management Support by Social Workers
target_population: Adults with Type 2 diabetes, particularly those with poor glycemic control and psychosocial barriers

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Immigrant and Refugee Health Support by Social Workers
target_population: Immigrants, refugees, and asylum seekers navigating the US healthcare and social service systems

expected_outcomes: Improved healthcare access and utilization, enhanced health insurance coverage, reduced barriers to care (language, cultural, financial), improved mental health and reduced trauma symptoms, increased social support and community integration, improved housing and employment stability, enhanced family well-being and child development, reduced health disparities among immigrant populations.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Suicide Risk Assessment and Safety Planning by Social Workers
target_population: Adolescents and adults at risk for suicide in healthcare, school, and community settings

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Chronic Kidney Disease Education and Support by Social Workers

implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive CKD education and psychosocial support program. Services include: 1) CKD education on disease progression, diet, and lifestyle modifications, 2) Depression and anxiety screening and intervention, 3) Advance care planning and treatment modality education (dialysis, transplant, conservative management), 4) Dialysis preparation and access planning, 5) Transplant evaluation and living donor education, 6) Medication adherence support and financial assistance, 7) Dietary counseling and fluid management, 8) Employment and disability benefits navigation, 9) Caregiver support and family education.
expected_outcomes: Improved CKD knowledge and self-management, enhanced shared decision-making for treatment modalities, increased advance directive completion, improved mental health outcomes, reduced depression and anxiety, enhanced quality of life, improved medication and dietary adherence, increased transplant referrals and living donor transplants, reduced hospitalizations, improved dialysis outcomes.
evidence_base: Cavanaugh et al. (2019). Patient-centered care for chronic kidney disease. Clinical Journal of the American Society of Nephrology, 14(1), 147-152.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for LGBTQ+ Affirming Care by Social Workers
target_population: LGBTQ+ individuals across the lifespan in healthcare and community settings
implementation_guidance: Implement LGBTQ+ affirming and culturally competent care practices. Components include: 1) Create welcoming environment with inclusive forms, signage, and policies, 2) Use correct names, pronouns, and gender-affirming language, 3) Comprehensive assessment of LGBTQ+-specific health needs and minority stress, 4) Mental health screening (depression, anxiety, suicidality) with awareness of disparities, 5) Substance use screening and intervention, 6) HIV/STI prevention and PrEP education, 7) Gender-affirming care coordination for transgender individuals, 8) Family acceptance and support interventions, 9) Connection to LGBTQ+ community resources and support groups.
expected_outcomes: Improved healthcare access and utilization among LGBTQ+ individuals, reduced healthcare avoidance and discrimination experiences, enhanced mental health outcomes and reduced suicidality, improved substance use outcomes, increased HIV/STI testing and prevention, improved family acceptance and support, enhanced quality of life and well-being, reduced health disparities for LGBTQ+ populations.
evidence_base: Streed et al. (2020). Assessing and addressing cardiovascular health in LGBTQ adults. Circulation, 142(19), e321-e332.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Opioid Use Disorder Care Coordination by Social Workers
target_population: Adults with opioid use disorder in primary care, emergency department, and community settings
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive opioid use disorder treatment and recovery support. Services include: 1) Opioid use screening and assessment using DSM-5 criteria, 2) Overdose risk assessment and naloxone distribution, 3) Medication for opioid use disorder (MOUD) initiation and coordination (buprenorphine, methadone, naltrexone), 4) Psychosocial treatment (counseling, CBT, contingency management), 5) Harm reduction education and syringe services, 6) Infectious disease screening (HIV, HCV, HBV), 7) Social determinants intervention, 8) Peer recovery support services, 9) Relapse prevention and long-term recovery planning.
expected_outcomes: Increased MOUD treatment initiation and retention (>60% retained at 6 months), reduced opioid use and cravings, decreased overdose deaths, improved mental health and quality of life, reduced infectious disease transmission, enhanced social functioning and employment, decreased criminal justice involvement, improved family relationships, long-term recovery and sustained remission.
evidence_base: Wakeman et al. (2020). Comparative effectiveness of different treatment pathways for opioid use disorder. JAMA Network Open, 3(2), e1920622.
